faq.label: Frequently asked
faq.title: Common questions
faq.subtitle: Everything you need to know before going solar.

items.q: What happens to panel efficiency after 10 years of operation?
items.a: Our premium photovoltaic modules have a degradation rate of just 0.4% per year — significantly below the industry average of 0.7%. After 10 years, your system will still operate at approximately 96% of its original capacity. After 25 years, we guarantee a minimum of 87.4% output.

items.q: How does the system perform during a full grid blackout?
items.a: Systems equipped with our hybrid inverter and battery package automatically switch to island mode within 20 milliseconds — fast enough that most appliances won't even register the outage. Standard grid-tied systems without storage will shut down per regulatory requirements.

items.q: How does the system perform during cloudy days or in winter?
items.a: Modern high-efficiency modules are highly sensitive to the full light spectrum, meaning they generate power even on overcast days. While production is lower in winter due to shorter days, our system architecture is optimized for low-light efficiency, ensuring a steady energy flow year-round.

items.q: Do I need to manually clean the panels or perform any maintenance?
items.a: Sunberg systems are designed for minimal maintenance. In most climates, rainfall is sufficient to keep panels clean. However, our technical support and modernization programs ensure that your system remains in peak condition with periodic expert health checks.

items.q: Can I integrate my electric vehicle (EV) charging into the solar ecosystem?
items.a: Absolutely. Our smart-home energy sync allows you to prioritize EV charging when solar production is at its peak. This "Solar-to-EV" logic ensures your car is powered by the cleanest and cheapest energy available, maximizing your savings.

items.q: How do you calculate ROI projections and what assumptions do you use?
items.a: Our projections use 10-year localized irradiance data from satellite sources, actual utility rate escalation trends (typically 3–5% annually), verified panel degradation curves, and your real consumption profile. We deliberately model conservative scenarios — our clients typically outperform projections by 8–12%.

items.q: What warranties are provided for the system components?
items.a: We only partner with Tier 1 manufacturers, providing a standard 25-year linear performance warranty for modules and 10-to-15 year warranties for inverters and storage systems. Additionally, Sunberg provides a comprehensive structural integrity guarantee for the entire installation.

items.q: Is it possible to expand the system capacity in the future?
items.a: Yes. Our modular architecture is designed for scalability. We can easily add more storage capacity or integrate additional panels as your energy needs evolve, ensuring your investment grows with you.

panelTypes.label: Photovoltaic Modules
panelTypes.title: The Core Engine of Independence
panelTypes.desc: Not all solar panels are created equal. Today's market offers a spectrum of advanced technologies, each with its own unique strengths, efficiencies, and price points. Explore how different cell architectures perform under real-world conditions to make an informed engineering decision.
panelTypes.introText: While there are many solar cell variations, the industry currently relies on three core technologies, each representing a different stage of photovoltaic evolution. Understanding the difference between PERC, TOPCon, and HJT is crucial for selecting the right system for your property.

technologies.name: PERC
technologies.desc: Passivated Emitter and Rear Cell (PERC) has been the industry standard for the past decade. It introduced a reflective layer on the back of the cell to capture unabsorbed light. While highly reliable and cost-effective, it is gradually reaching its theoretical efficiency limit.

technologies.name: TOPCon
technologies.desc: Tunnel Oxide Passivated Contact (TOPCon) represents the current sweet spot between cost and high performance. By adding an ultra-thin oxide layer, it significantly reduces electron recombination, offering higher efficiency and better performance in hot climates compared to PERC.

technologies.name: HJT
technologies.desc: Heterojunction Technology (HJT) is the premium tier of solar engineering. It combines crystalline silicon with layers of thin-film amorphous silicon, resulting in unparalleled efficiency, the lowest degradation rates, and the best temperature coefficient on the market. Ideal for maximizing yield in limited spaces.

inverterTypes.label: Power Inverters
inverterTypes.title: The Brains of the System
inverterTypes.desc: An inverter is essential for converting the DC power generated by your panels into usable AC power. Explore the different inverter architectures to find the best match for your energy goals.

technologies.name: String Inverters
technologies.desc: String inverters are a cost-effective standard for systems with uniform sunlight exposure. All panels are connected in a series, making it highly efficient for unshaded roofs.

technologies.name: Microinverters
technologies.desc: Microinverters are installed on each individual panel. They optimize performance panel-by-panel, ensuring that shading on one module doesn't affect the rest of the system.

technologies.name: Hybrid Inverters
technologies.desc: Hybrid inverters can manage both solar power and battery storage simultaneously. They are the ideal choice if you plan to add energy storage for nighttime use or backup power.

batteryStorage.label: Battery Storage
batteryStorage.title: Power Through the Night
batteryStorage.desc: Battery storage allows you to achieve true energy independence by storing excess solar power during the day to use at night or during grid outages. Discover the most advanced energy storage solutions available today.

technologies.name: LFP (Lithium Iron Phosphate)
technologies.desc: LFP batteries are the industry gold standard for stationary storage. They offer an incredible lifespan, superior thermal stability, and deep discharge capabilities, making them incredibly safe and reliable over decades of daily use.

technologies.name: NMC (Nickel Manganese Cobalt)
technologies.desc: NMC batteries provide higher energy density, meaning they pack more power into a smaller physical footprint. Ideal for installations where space is severely limited, though they typically have a slightly shorter cycle life than LFP.

technologies.name: Modular Racks
technologies.desc: Modular rack systems allow for effortless scalability. You can start with a basic capacity and easily add more battery modules later as your home's energy consumption grows or you purchase an electric vehicle.

safetyAndFuses.label: Safety & Fuses
safetyAndFuses.title: Absolute Protection
safetyAndFuses.desc: Solar systems generate high voltages. Our protection mechanisms ensure absolute safety for your home, the grid, and first responders in case of an emergency.

technologies.name: Rapid Shutdown
technologies.desc: Rapid shutdown devices instantly drop the system voltage to safe levels in case of a grid outage or emergency. This is a critical safety feature required by modern electrical codes to protect firefighters.

technologies.name: Surge Protection
technologies.desc: Surge Protection Devices (SPDs) shield your delicate solar inverters and home appliances from sudden voltage spikes caused by nearby lightning strikes or grid fluctuations.

technologies.name: DC Isolators
technologies.desc: High-quality DC isolator switches allow for safe manual disconnection of the solar arrays from the inverter during maintenance or troubleshooting, preventing electrical arcing.

mountingSystems.label: Mounting Systems
mountingSystems.title: The Foundation
mountingSystems.desc: A solar installation is only as reliable as the structure that holds it. We use premium, weather-resistant mounting hardware engineered for decades of stability, ensuring your panels stay secure in any climate.

technologies.name: Pitched Roof Mounts
technologies.desc: Designed to perfectly integrate with the existing angle of your roof. These low-profile mounts provide excellent structural integrity while maintaining the aesthetic appeal of your home.

technologies.name: Flat Roof Ballasted
technologies.desc: For flat roofs, we utilize ballasted mounting systems. Instead of penetrating the roof membrane, these mounts use heavy concrete blocks to secure the panels, eliminating the risk of leaks.

technologies.name: Ground Mounts
technologies.desc: When roof space is limited or shaded, ground mounts are the perfect alternative. They can be optimally angled and positioned anywhere on your property for maximum solar yield.

connectionSchemes.label: System Architecture
connectionSchemes.title: How the Energy Flows
connectionSchemes.desc: Understand how different system configurations distribute and manage power based on your unique goals.

schemes.name: Grid-Tied
schemes.desc: The most common setup. Your panels power your home, and excess energy is sent to the grid. No batteries required.

schemes.name: Off-Grid
schemes.desc: Complete energy independence. You are disconnected from the utility grid entirely. Requires significant battery storage.

schemes.name: Hybrid
schemes.desc: The best of both worlds. Connected to the grid for backup, but utilizes battery storage to capture excess solar power.
